_meta.indication: EVRYSDI is indicated for the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) in patients 2 months of age and older

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, single-arm, two-part, multicenter study; Part 1 served as the pivotal efficacy study for infantile-onset SMA
pivotal_trials.population: Infants with confirmed 5q-autosomal recessive Type 1 SMA with two SMN2 gene copies
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of infants sitting without support for 5 seconds (Item 22 of the BSID-III gross motor scale) after 12 months of treatment
pivotal_trials.result: 33% (7/21) of all patients and 41% (7/17) in the high-dose cohort achieved sitting without support for 5 seconds after 12 months; 85% were alive without permanent ventilation (event-free survival) at Month 12

nct_ctgov.title: Investigate Safety, Tolerability, PK, PD and Efficacy of Risdiplam (RO7034067) in Infants With Type1 Spinal Muscular Atrophy

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.phase: Two-part randomized controlled trial (Part 2 controlled portion pivotal)
pivotal_trials.design: Two-part, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study; patients randomized 2:1 to risdiplam or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Non-ambulatory patients age 2 to 25 years with genetic confirmation of SMN1 loss of function and clinical symptoms of Type 2 or Type 3 SMA
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in the Motor Function Measure 32 (MFM32) total score at Month 12
pivotal_trials.result: MFM32 change from baseline at Month 12: LS Mean +1.36 (risdiplam) vs -0.19 (placebo); treatment difference 1.55 (95% CI 0.30, 2.81); p=0.0156

nct_ctgov.title: A Study to Investigate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics and Efficacy of Risdiplam (RO7034067) in Type 2 and 3 Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) Participants

key_safety: Most frequent adverse events (greater with risdiplam than placebo): upper respiratory tract infection (32%), pyrexia (21%), headache (20%), diarrhea (17%), and rash (13%). Most frequent serious AE difference was pneumonia (7.5% risdiplam vs 1.7% placebo).
target_moa: Risdiplam is a survival of motor neuron 2 (SMN2)-directed RNA splicing modifier that increases exon 7 inclusion in SMN2 mRNA transcripts and production of full-length SMN protein

rems.type: The Division of Risk Management concluded that a REMS is not necessary for risdiplam

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not referred to an advisory committee because outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues

description.text: Expanded indication to include patients from birth (younger pediatric population) based on Study BP39056

citations.quote: Include patients from birth and older in the Evrysdi postmarketing surveillance previously requested in the NDA Approval letter dated August 7, 2020, and in the Complete Response letter dated March 23, 2020, for all reported cases of vasculitis or suspected vasculitis and for oral mucosal ulceration or other non-herpetic oral lesions, including chelitis, and for serious adverse events in the skin, including alopecia, rash, skin erosion, and exfoliation after exposure to Evrysdi.

summary.text: Risdiplam (Evrysdi), a new molecular entity small-molecule SMN2 splicing modifier, was granted Fast Track (04/05/2017), Orphan Drug (01/04/2017), Priority Review, and Rolling Submission (05/30/2019) designations. The NDA was received September 24, 2019 and approved without an advisory committee meeting for the treatment of SMA in patients 2 months of age and older.

citations.quote: The FDA granted risdiplam Fast Track (04/05/2017), Orphan Drug (01/04/2017), Priority review, and Rolling submission (05/30/2019) designations.
Risdiplam is a new molecular entity (NME) containing no previously approved active ingredient (including any ester or salt of the active ingredient).
This new drug application provides for the use of Evrysdi (risdiplam) for oral solution for the treatment of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) in patients 2 months of age and older.
